cornerCallouts: Drivers need to be precise through Old Hall Corner, carrying good speed without running wide on exit is crucial for a quick lap time.
Clay Hill is a real test of commitment; the drivers have to trust the grip and carry plenty of momentum through this blind crest.
Negotiating the Hislops chicane requires pinpoint accuracy; too much kerb and you risk upsetting the car, not enough and you lose valuable time.
The run down to Druids is a key overtaking opportunity, but drivers must be wary of defending too aggressively and compromising their exit.
Lakeside is a classic corner, demanding respect and rewarding bravery. Get it right, and you'll gain significant time.
The double-apex of Knickerbrook is a real crowd-pleaser, as the drivers wrestle their cars through this complex sequence of turns.
A good exit from Shell Oils Corner is vital, setting up the long run down to Island Bend and the next overtaking opportunity.
Cascades is one of the most challenging corners on the circuit; the drivers need to be precise with their braking and steering inputs to avoid a trip into the gravel.
strategyPoints: Tire degradation will be a major factor on this 4.4km Historic layout. The abrasive surface will punish the tires, especially the front left.
The pit window here is relatively short, so teams will need to be precise with their timing to avoid losing track position.
Fuel consumption will be a concern, especially in the early stages of the race when the drivers are pushing hard. Fuel saving might be needed later on.
With limited overtaking opportunities, track position is key. A good start and a well-executed pit stop strategy are essential.
The undulating nature of the circuit puts a lot of stress on the suspension, so teams will need to monitor their cars carefully for any signs of damage.
The Historic layout's mix of high-speed corners and tight chicanes means finding the right balance between downforce and drag is crucial.
Oulton Park's narrow track and lack of run-off areas means safety car periods are common, so teams need to be prepared to react quickly to changing circumstances.
Undercut or overcut? The teams will be crunching the numbers to see if they can gain an advantage in the pits. It's going to be fascinating to watch.
weatherCommentary: The Cheshire weather is notoriously unpredictable. A sudden downpour can quickly turn this race on its head.
That wind swirling through the trees could become a real factor, particularly through the faster sections of the circuit.

The cloud cover is patchy, so track temperature could fluctuate significantly throughout the race, impacting tire performance.
That mist hanging over the Cheshire hills could roll in and create visibility problems, especially in the early morning sessions.
